newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN UNION CHIEF MAY QUIT OVER COACH ROW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN UNION CHIEF MAY QUIT OVER COACH ROW.

text.p: Belgian soccer union president Michel D'Hooghe said on Friday he might quit over the way the union handled the nomination of new national coach Georges Leekens.

"One of my closest assistants thought he should leak it to the press and I cannot live with that...I take this very seriously and if it becomes clear the executive committee believes the president did something wrong, I'm willing to lay down my mandate," D'Hooghe told BRTN radio.

Leekens was coach of surprise first division leaders Mouscron when the union approached him to replace Wilfried Van Moer, who was blamed for Belgium's humiliating 3-0 home defeat by the Netherlands in a World Cup qualifier last month.
But the news of his nomination was leaked to a newspaper on Tuesday, forcing the union to sack Van Moer prematurely.

Belgian newspapers said D'Hooghe had been led to believe that Mouscron would not object to the departure of Leekens from the first division newcomers, who have opened up a four-point lead over title holders Club Brugge.
The case is particularly embarrassing for the soccer union as the affair broke just before a crucial match between Mouscron and Anderlecht, who were meeting later on Friday.
Leekens first proposed to Mouscron that he should combine the jobs of national and club coach until the end of the season and later said he would stay until after the Anderlecht game.

But Mouscron, who learned of Leekens's contract with the soccer union only through the media, sacked him on Thursday with immediate effect and slammed the union for the way it had lured their coach away at such a delicate time.
"Suppose Leekens was still coaching us for the Anderlecht game, it would have meant that we approved the trick the union played on us," manager Willy Verhoost told Het Volk newspaper.
Mouscron also told the soccer union it wanted to be compensated for the loss of its coach, whose contract ran for a further three seasons.
"The soccer union will not get off so easily," Mouscron chairman Jean-Pierre Detremmerie said.

"Leekens had a five-year contract. We hope to reach a financial settlement of this case with the union within a week in a friendly way. If we're not on the same wavelength we'll be forced to take legal steps."
Verhoost alleged the union would never have dared to sign Leekens if he had been coaching Club Brugge or Anderlecht, Belgium's two soccer powerhouses.
"In full battle for the title we're being decapitated, precisely by the mother (the union) of all clubs. Incredible," Verhoost said.
